To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
on the job training is effective in increasing the probability to find a job, but off the job training is not.

(1) on-the-job training increases the probability to find employment, (2) on-the-job-training increases the probability to get a permanent contract, and (3) the impact of off-the-job training is negligible, and it is mostly due to a lock-in effect
- PIPOL has a positive impact on the probability to find a job, but no impact on the probability of finding a permanent job.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of P.I.P.O.L., an integrated program of labor policies, on employment integration of benefit receivers.
the impact of active labor policy on the employment integration process of benefit recipients.
the evaluation of the PIPOL program, which is an integrated program of labor policies implemented in France since 2013.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the program had no impact on the probability to be employed, while it had a positive impact on the probability of finding a permanent job and on the probability to have at least one contract in the period 2016-2018.
active labor policies work when they generate work related competences.
the program has been successful in improving the labor market outcomes of the beneficiaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
active labor market policies are effective in increasing labor market participation, but not in reducing unemployment.
PIPOL is a successful program, but it is not successful for everyone.

PIPOL has had a significant impact on the labor market performance of young benefit recipients, but it has not had any impact for those who are not in the labor force, or who do not have any job related competences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of active labor policies on employment outcomes is not homogeneous across different types of interventions and recipients.
the program is not a panacea, but that it can be a powerful instrument to improve the employment integration of the most disadvantaged.
the impact of the program is not uniform across the population.
